localDifficulty.difficultyReason: Introduce a midpoint on the diagonal and prove the midpoint lemma from a new SAS construction before combining two half-base lengths into a symbolic result.

content.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a trapezium with parallel sides $AB$ and $CD$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the midpoints of $AD$ and $BC$ respectively. Let $k$ be the length of $EF$. Let $AB=a$ and $CD=c$.

answer.worked:
First prove the midpoint lemma. In triangle $XYZ$, let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $XY,XZ$. Extend $MN$ to $H$ with $NH=MN$. Triangles $XNM$ and $ZNH$ are congruent by SAS: equal half-sides, equal segments and vertically opposite included angles. Hence $XM=ZH$ and $XM\parallel ZH$. Since $XM=MY$, quadrilateral $YMHZ$ has one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel, so it is a parallelogram. Thus $MH=YZ$, $MN=YZ/2$ and $MN\parallel YZ$.

Let $G$ be the midpoint of diagonal $BD$. Apply the lemma in triangle $DAB$: $EG=a/2$ and $EG\parallel AB$. Apply it in triangle $BCD$: $GF=c/2$ and $GF\parallel CD$. Since $AB\parallel CD$, the points $E,G,F$ are collinear, with $G$ between $E$ and $F$.
$$k=EF=EG+GF=\frac a2+\frac c2=\frac{a+c}{2}.$$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. A line through the vertex $A$, parallel to the diagonal $BD$, meets $CD$ (extended) at $E$. Show that the area of triangle $BCE$ equals the area of $ABCD$.

answer.worked:
The vertices $A$ and $E$ lie on a line parallel to $BD$, so triangles $ABD$ and $EBD$ have the same base $BD$ and the same perpendicular height. Thus $[ABD]=[EBD]$. Since $C,D,E$ are collinear with $D$ between $C$ and $E$,
$$\begin{aligned}[BCE]&=[BCD]+[BDE]\\&=[BCD]+[ABD]\\&=[ABCD].\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Let $ABCDE$ be a convex pentagon. Construct a triangle with the same area as this pentagon.

answer.short: Construct $P$ on $CD$ produced with $BP\parallel AC$. Then construct $Q$ on $DE$ produced with $AQ\parallel PE$. Triangle $PDQ$ has the required area.
answer.worked:
Draw diagonal $AC$. Through $B$ draw a line parallel to $AC$, meeting $CD$ produced beyond $C$ at $P$. Triangles $ABC$ and $APC$ have equal area, sharing base $AC$ with their third vertices on a parallel line. Replacing triangle $ABC$ by $APC$ turns convex pentagon $ABCDE$ into equal-area quadrilateral $APDE$.

Apply part a to quadrilateral $APDE$: through $A$ draw a line parallel to diagonal $PE$, meeting $DE$ produced at $Q$. Triangle $PDQ$ has the area of $APDE$, hence the original pentagon. Keep the construction lines and mark both pairs of parallel lines.

content.prompt: $OA$ and $OB$ are perpendicular radii of a circle $C_1$ ($OA\perp OB$). A circle $C_2$ is drawn with diameter $AB$ as shown. Find the ratio of the area of the blue crescent to the area of the grey segment.

answer.worked:
Let $OA=OB=r$. Since $OA\perp OB$, in the quarter-circle, triangle $OAB$ has area $r^2/2$ and the quarter-sector has area $\pi r^2/4$. The grey segment therefore has area $G=(\pi-2)r^2/4$.

By Pythagoras, $AB^2=2r^2$, so the semicircle on diameter $AB$ has area $\pi AB^2/8=\pi r^2/4$. Subtract the grey segment to find the blue crescent:
$$\begin{aligned}B&=\frac{\pi r^2}{4}-\frac{(\pi-2)r^2}{4}=\frac{r^2}{2}\\B:G&=\frac{r^2}{2}:\frac{(\pi-2)r^2}{4}\\&=1:\left(\frac\pi2-1\right).\end{aligned}$$

entries.description: A foam drink-can holder is in the shape of a cylinder. The inside radius is 5.5 cm and the inside height is 11 cm. The foam is 1 cm thick and forms the curved surface of the cylinder. The base is cut out of foam 1 cm thick.
Calculate the volume inside the cylinder in cubic centimetres.
Calculate the volume of foam in the drink-can holder in cubic centimetres.
If a cylindrical drink can perfectly fills the holder, find the total surface area of the exposed foam in square centimetres.

Open cylindrical foam holder shown in perspective, with concentric elliptical top rims, outer vertical sides and a thick circular base. Dashed red lines show concealed inner sides and lower circular boundaries. No dimension labels are printed.

presentation.meaning: Shows the hollow cylinder, open top and closed foam base.

entries.description: Two related rectangular-prism problems.
A rectangular prism has faces of area 66, 48 and 88. Find the volume of the prism.
A box in the shape of a rectangular prism is strapped as shown. The length of the straps are 100, 60 and 80.
Find the dimensions of the box.
Find the volume of the box.

Perspective rectangular box with three perpendicular closed strap loops: one horizontal loop and two vertical loops. Visible strap sections are blue filled; concealed sections have red dashed boundaries. Dimension arrows label front width x, receding depth y and vertical height z. No strap is individually assigned a numerical length.

presentation.meaning: Each strap encircles one pair of box dimensions; preserve all three loop paths and x, y, z labels.

entries.description: Let ABCD be a trapezium with parallel sides AB and CD. Let E and F be the midpoints of AD and BC respectively. Let k be the length of EF. Let AB = a and CD = c.
Prove that k = (a + c)/2.
Deduce that the area of the trapezium is kh, where h is the distance between the parallel sides.

Trapezium ABCD with A upper left, B upper right, C lower right and D lower left. AB is labelled a; CD is labelled c; matching arrowheads mark these sides parallel. E and F lie halfway along AD and BC, joined by EF labelled k. Double ticks mark AE = ED; triple ticks mark BF = FC. A vertical double-headed arrow outside the right side marks perpendicular height h between dotted horizontal extensions of AB and CD.
Related equal-area construction problems.
Let ABCD be a convex quadrilateral. A line through the vertex A, parallel to the diagonal BD, meets CD (extended) at E. Show that the area of triangle BCE equals the area of ABCD.
